script: TB +2.5 and a 38 total point to a tight, low-event game: Pittsburgh can stay on schedule with Jaylen Warren (49 carries, 321 rush yards over weeks 3-5) rather than asking Aaron Rodgers to win it through the air, and Tampa Bay answers with Bucky Irving (52 carries, 272 yards) instead of a chase script. Touch volume is already decided — Warren also has 17 targets, Irving only 7 — so the backs, not the 200-air-yard receivers, are the usage winners in a 38-point game.
who_goes_off: Bucky Irving is the Tampa Bay piece who should go off: 272 rush yards on 52 carries (5.23 YPC, 90.7 per game) into a Pittsburgh front that has allowed 4.21 YPC and 13 runs of 10-plus yards. Jaylen Warren is the Pittsburgh counterpart at 321 rush yards plus 169 receiving yards, and Tampa Bay's 41% blitz rate pushes a struggling Rodgers into the checkdowns Warren already lives on (–21 air yards, 17 targets).
weak_spot: Tampa Bay's pass defense leaks in the middle — 9.25 YPA on 32 attempts versus 6.59 on the left (78 att) and 6.48 on the right (56 att) — so the matchup is linebackers, nickel, and safeties, not the outside corners holding DK Metcalf to 158 yards on 243 air yards. Pittsburgh's leak is the run front (4.21 YPC, 13 gains of 10-plus) against a Tampa Bay rush defense that has allowed only 3.61 YPC and 9 runs of 10-plus, which is why Irving's yards are the cleaner explosive path than a pure Warren rush number.
injury_fallout: No injury report is in the pre-kickoff data, so no absence reallocates touches. The carry splits already show the hierarchy: Warren 49 of Pittsburgh's recent rushes (Homer 3, Rodgers 3, Nichols 2) and Irving 52 of Tampa Bay's (Daniels 14, Gainwell 10, Tucker 8).
qb_vs_blitz: Aaron Rodgers is –0.38 EPA per dropback vs the blitz (n=52) against –0.01 with no blitz, and Tampa Bay blitzes 41%, which caps Metcalf (18 targets, 243 air yards, 158 yards) and Roman Wilson (234 air yards, 134 yards) and feeds Warren's dump-offs. Baker Mayfield is also worse vs pressure (–0.21 EPA, n=71) than without it (–0.10), but Pittsburgh blitzes only 27%, so the sharper Tampa Bay attack is Irving on the ground, not forcing Mayfield into that split.

picks.why: Irving has 272 rush yards on 52 carries over three games (90.7 per game, 5.23 YPC) against a 64.5 line, and Pittsburgh has allowed 4.21 YPC plus 13 runs of 10-plus in five games. Seventeen carries at even a regressed 4.2 YPC projects near 71, and TB +2.5 with a 38 total keeps Tampa Bay in a rushing script; his 22 receiving yards on 7 targets are too thin to prefer the 10.5 rec line or to need the 79.5 rush+rec number.

Warren is at 321 rush yards plus 169 receiving yards over three games (about 163 rush+rec per game) on 49 carries and 17 targets versus a 91.5 line. Tampa Bay's 3.61 YPC and only 9 runs of 10-plus can pin the pure rush total near 60.5, so this is the combined number: Rodgers at –0.38 EPA vs a 41% blitz funnels checkdowns to a back already at –21 air yards and 56 receiving yards per game, and 91.5 is only about 4.6 yards per touch on a 20-touch role.
